dedupe_keys.name: coupled european heavy industry and electricity hydrogen energy system model for decarbonisation planning mines paris 2024

description: This model couples an industry model covering the main heavy industry sectors of six European countries with an energy system model of electricity and hydrogen for fifteen European regions, the EU-15, split into eleven zones, to study how decarbonising industry and the energy system affect each other. Policy scenarios under different conditions show that industrial decarbonisation raises electricity and hydrogen demand considerably; the extra electricity comes mostly from renewables, hydrogen is largely met by blue hydrogen when fossil fuels are allowed and renewables are short, prices rise with large regional differences, and the EU-15 electricity mix stays above 85% renewable in every scenario. It was developed by Quentin Raillard-Cazanove, Thibaut Knibiehly and Robin Girard and posted on arXiv on 30 October 2024. Coverage is Western Europe. The preprint is available free online; only the arXiv licence link is shown and no code is linked. Caveats: it is a preprint, the exact sectors and technology data are in the full text, which was not read, and results depend on scenario assumptions. For simulation it shows how industrial electrification and hydrogen use feed back on power and hydrogen infrastructure planning, useful for scenarios of chemical, steel and cement plants in energy transitions. It is related to the RCI net-zero chemical industry 2050 scenario review record in this catalogue.
